outcome_detail: Filed June 28, 2024 in the 56th Circuit Court for Eaton County; survived a state motion to dismiss in April 2025 (state attorneys planned to appeal) and remained active as of April 2026 coverage, which described ongoing litigation including the plaintiff's allegation that Lt. Col. Aimee Brimacombe committed perjury in an affidavit filed in the case. The plaintiff separately prevailed twice in arbitration over her terminations and received back pay in May 2025 described as a 'MAKE WHOLE SETTLEMENT,' but the lawsuit itself is unresolved.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges have been reported against the supervisor or other MSP personnel accused of harassment. In 2026 Moryc filed a complaint alleging perjury by Lt. Col. Aimee Brimacombe over a March 2025 affidavit in this civil case; no charges have been reported. Moryc herself was criminally charged over an October 2020 incident and entered a no-contest plea to two assault-and-battery counts; her suit characterizes the investigations and charges against her as retaliatory.
incident_date_approx: Alleged conduct from November 2016 through her August 2021 termination, with alleged retaliation continuing thereafter
description: Former Michigan State Police trooper Megan Moryc sued the Michigan State Police on June 28, 2024, in the 56th Circuit Court for Eaton County, alleging gender discrimination, sexual harassment, and retaliation in violation of Michigan's Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act, within what she described as a 'Big Boys' Club' culture. According to the complaint, a supervisor to whom she was assigned in November 2016 began sexually harassing her almost immediately, repeatedly propositioning her for dates and sex while holding authority over her probationary status; the suit also describes rampant harassment by other officers, including condoms placed in her backpack and pornography viewed in the workplace. Moryc alleges she was denied promotions three times despite outranking the selected candidates, that MSP refused to investigate her assault claims, and that she faced repeated investigations, criminal charges, and two terminations in retaliation for reporting harassment and for assisting another agency's officer in filing a criminal complaint against an MSP trooper who allegedly secretly recorded consensual sex. Arbitrators twice ruled in her favor on her terminations. The suit, which arose from allegations aired in an extensive WLNS 6 News investigative series, survived a motion to dismiss in April 2025 and remains pending; Moryc has more recently alleged that a senior MSP official made false sworn statements in the case.
notes: Related suit from same scandal: see companion record rec-5b (September 2025 federal suit by the same plaintiff against MSP leadership, W.D. Mich.). Duplicate record rec-74 (same suit) was merged into this record and deleted.
